key_insight: Low-rank biases in training dynamics can make dynamical systems-based generative models collapse or learn smaller modes too slowly to capture them within a fixed training budget.
engineering_relevance: For flow- and diffusion-based generators, missing modes may reflect either stable collapse or slow feature learning, making the distinction important when diagnosing training.
method: Express gradient flow for a general class of stochastic differential equations as compositions of linear operators.
Relate these operators to low-rank biases in generative learning.
Analyze collapse mechanisms in variational inference and flow-matching tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stable collapsed fixed points and sequential feature learning in variational inference and flow-matching settings, but provides no datasets or quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how broadly these mechanisms apply to practical architectures or discrete-time training.
paper_title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
